@graph.headline: How Much Does a Wood Fence Cost in Michigan? A Complete 2026 Pricing Guide for Oakland County Homeowners
@graph.description: Wondering how much a wood fence costs in Michigan in 2026? This complete pricing guide breaks down material costs, labor rates, permit fees, and ROI for Oakland County homeowners — from real local experts, not national averages.

mainEntity.name: How much does a 6-foot privacy fence cost in Michigan?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a standard 6-foot privacy fence in Oakland County, expect to pay $30 to $50 per linear foot installed in 2026. Pressure-treated pine runs $30-$35 installed; cedar runs $40-$50 installed. On an average quarter-acre lot (150-200 ft), that's $4,500 to $10,000 total.

mainEntity.name: What is the most affordable wood fence material in Michigan?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pressure-treated pine is the most affordable wood fence material for Michigan's climate. At $30-$35 per linear foot installed, it offers the best balance of durability and cost. It handles Michigan's freeze-thaw cycles well when properly installed.

mainEntity.name: Does a fence increase home value enough to justify the cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, typically. A well-built, well-maintained wood fence recovers 50-70% of its cost in increased home value, according to real estate data for the Metro Detroit market. Homes with fenced yards also tend to sell 2-5 days faster.

mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to replace a fence in Michigan?

acceptedAnswer.text: Full fence replacement costs $35-$55 per linear foot, which includes removing and disposing of the old fence and installing a new one. The additional cost over new installation is $5-$8 per foot for removal and disposal.

mainEntity.name: What is the labor cost for fence installation in Oakland County?

acceptedAnswer.text: Labor for fence installation in Oakland County runs $12-$18 per linear foot in 2026. This covers digging 42-inch post holes below the frost line, concrete setting, leveling, alignment, and gate installation. Labor accounts for roughly 40-50% of your total fence cost.

mainEntity.name: How long does a wood fence last in Michigan?

acceptedAnswer.text: A properly installed pressure-treated pine fence lasts 10-15 years with staining every 2-3 years. Cedar lasts 15-20 years. Given that the cost works out to roughly $300-$700 per year over the fence's lifespan for a standard lot, it is a worthwhile investment.

mainEntity.name: Should I stain my fence to protect my investment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Absolutely. Staining or sealing a new pressure-treated fence within the first year is the single most important thing you can do to extend its life. Untreated wood grays, cracks, and absorbs moisture. Staining costs $300-$1,000 for an average lot and adds years of life.
